candidate_sources.title: Characterization of Gnomoniopsis idaeicola, the Causal Agent of Canker and Wilting of Blackberry in Serbia | Plant Disease (APS)
candidate_sources.snippet: Gnomoniopsis idaeicola found to be the causal agent of cane canker and wilting in Rubus orchards. The holotype of G. idaeicola was collected on raspberry (Rubus idaeus L.) in Finland in 1886.

candidate_sources.title: Gnomonia Leaf Blotch and Stem-End Rot of Strawberry | NC State Extension Publications
candidate_sources.snippet: Gnomonia comari is a fungal plant pathogen. Symptoms consist of tan to gray leaf lesions developing along the margin of leaflets; leaf blotches are irregular and may be surrounded by a purple border. A key diagnostic feature is the presence of tiny, brown to black fungal fruiting bodies in the gray blotches.

candidate_sources.title: Resistance to cane and foliar diseases in red raspberry (Rubus idaeus) and related species | Euphytica
candidate_sources.snippet: Resistance to cane and foliar diseases in red raspberry (Rubus idaeus) and related species, covering cane canker and spot pathogens affecting Rubus idaeus.

candidate_sources.title: Cane spot | Agrobase
candidate_sources.snippet: Cane spot disease of raspberry/Rubus, describing leaf and cane spot symptoms and management.

candidate_sources.title: Late leaf rust on raspberry | UMN Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Symptoms of late leaf rust appear in late July or early August first on lower foliage with small chlorotic or yellow areas; yellow-orange powdery pustules on leaf surfaces and on fruit. Causes decreased plant vigour, early defoliation, and increased winter frost sensitivity. Management: plant disease-free stock, maintain air circulation, full sun, drip irrigation, fungicides.

candidate_sources.title: Late Leaf Rust of Red Raspberries | Ohioline (Ohio State University Extension)
candidate_sources.snippet: Late leaf rust of red raspberries (Rubus idaeus) caused by Pucciniastrum americanum. Small yellow spots turning brown and yellow-orange powdery pustules on adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces and light yellow/orange pustules on fruits. Includes pathogen biology and management recommendations.

candidate_sources.title: Raspberry (Rubus spp.)-Yellow Rust | Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks
candidate_sources.snippet: Yellow rust caused by Phragmidium rubi-idaei. Leaf infections in spring create yellowish spotting on upper leaf surface (spermagonia), then aecia in a ring; orange to yellow uredinia on leaf undersides in June-July. Severely affected leaves dry, die, and drop prematurely. Overwinters as teliospores on leaves; leaf wetness needed for infection.

candidate_sources.title: Yellow Rust of Red Raspberry / UC Statewide IPM Program (UC IPM)
candidate_sources.snippet: Yellow rust (Phragmidium rubi-idaei) of red raspberry. Yellow to orange spots and pustules on leaves; aecia and uredinia described; teliospores overwinter on fallen leaves. Provides symptom, disease cycle, and management information for caneberries.

candidate_sources.title: Phragmidium rubi-idaei (raspberry yellow rust) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet for Phragmidium rubi-idaei, the cause of raspberry yellow rust, covering distribution, host range, symptoms, biology, and management on Rubus idaeus.
